newsitem.title: SPAIN: Lufthansa sees Iberia cargo up 10pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa sees Iberia cargo up 10pct in 96.

text.p: Deutsche Lufthansa AG's ex-Iberia cargo business should grow around 10 or 11 percent in volume terms this year, the airline's director general for France, Spain and Portugal said on Thursday.

Average growth has been between three and five percent in recent years, Ulrich Link said, but this year the total volume from Spain and Portugal is likely to reach around 14,500 tonnes from just over 13,000 in 1995.
"Barcelona is performing well and Bilbao business is very strong," Link told Reuters in an interview.
Lufthansa carries a wide range of cargo from the Iberian peninsula, most of which (80 percent) travels by truck to Frankfurt and only around 20 percent goes by air.
Express items travel on a United Parcel Service freighter from Madrid or Oporto every night to Cologne where both carriers have their express hubs.

Lufthansa's strongest cargo routes from Spain are to the Far East, mainly Hong Kong, Seoul and Tokyo. It has a small share of the South Atlantic market, where Iberia, TAP-Air Portugal and the Latin American carriers predominate, and does little on the North Atlantic.
"The rates are so low on the North Atlantic that for us to take goods via Frankfurt would mean a loss," Link said. "We'd like to participate, but not at those rates."
Rates quoted for 100 kilos minimum ex-Madrid to New York are typically around 150 pesetas a kilo but market sources say prices of around 100 pesetas are available.
Lufthansa also carries an increasing amount of cargo from the Iberian peninsula to Scandinavia and the CIS.

Its partnership with Scandinavian Airlines System will be closer from December 1 when it takes over as general sales agent for SAS's cargo business from Spain, probably extending to include Portugal too in the future, said Jurgen Siebenrock, the German flag carrier's cargo manager in Madrid.

Lufthansa, being German-based with a subsequently high cost base tends to have higher tariffs than its Spanish or Latin American competitors in Spain, would like to expand its premium and express business, Seibenrock added.

Rates from Spain have been steady this year compared with last and are unlikely to rise in the near future, Lufthansa said. Competition is increasing constantly as worldwide air freight capacity grows.

Lufthansa is in the process of selling its DC-8 freighters but will lease some of them back as business demands between now and 1998 when the first of five McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighters it has ordered is due to be delivered.
The others will follow in the subsequent years, Link said.
